title: Enhancing the low-carbon performance for municipal wastewater treatment through high-rate activated sludge-three-stage constructed wetland system: Water quality, energy recovery and carbon emissions reduction
description: Biological-ecological coupling processes are attracting increasing interest for low-carbon performance in municipal wastewater treatment. However, the effectiveness for reducing carbon emissions remains vague. In this study, three lab-scale high-rate activated sludge (HRAS) formulas operating at different dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations were coupled with a three-stage constructed wetland (TCW) system, and the performances of these HRAS-TCW systems were investigated in terms of nutrient removal, energy recovery, and greenhouse gas emissions. The results revealed that, compared with the systems with medium (HRAS-TCWM) and high (HRAS-TCWH) DO concentrations, the low DO concentration (HRAS-TCWL) system achieved the highest carbon recovery, with 49.3% of energy consumption compensated by the electrical energy produced from methane production. By improving the function of the TCW module, the three HRAS-TCW systems achieved satisfactory treatment performance, and the HRAS-TCWL system achieved the lowest CO2-eq emissions via the optimized redox environment. Moreover, the HRAS-TCWL system achieved the highest recovered energy, with its contribution to carbon neutrality reaching 35.4%, which was higher than that of the other two systems (25.8-30.3%), further coordinating the nexus of water quality-energy recovery-carbon emissions when treating wastewater with a low carbon-nitrogen ratio. Analysis of the microbial community structure showed that the optimized redox environment led to distinctive microbial communities in each unit of three HRAS-TCW systems, which facilitated simultaneous nutrient removal enhancement and carbon emission reduction. Overall, the HRAS-TCW process studied here provides a feasible low-carbon design and operation for municipal wastewater treatment.
samples: Microbe sample from Ferruginibacter sp. HRAS
Microbe sample from Zoogloea sp. CWF
Microbe sample from Thauera sp. CWM
Microbe sample from Nitrospira sp. CWB
